atoms.title: Combinational timing and WB reset
atoms.definition: All outputs except the three WB outputs change combinationally with the current inputs. A clk rising edge updates dc3_wb_data and dc3_wb_addr, unconditionally sampling dc2_message_data/address respectively, even when reset=1 or message_valid=0; these two are not reset. dc3_wb_enable is immediately cleared to 0 on a reset rising edge; it remains 0 on every rising edge while reset is high, and after deassertion it takes the current processing condition on every rising edge: 1 when the selected state is MN_A and the message is PUTM and source equals the selected owner, and 0 otherwise. This condition is not gated by dc2_message_valid. Sample after 1ns of settling following combinational input changes; sample WB 1ns after a rising edge, and asynchronous reset 1ns after assertion between edges. At startup, reset first and pass through at least one clock edge; WB data/address are undefined before the first edge. A high reset pulse shorter than one cycle and not spanning a rising edge also clears WB enable; reset does not force other outputs to zero.

atoms.title: Metadata selection, pending, and bitmaps
atoms.definition: The priority for selecting state/sharers/owner is TSHR hit, cache hit, replacement metadata when neither of the first two applies and the message is REPLACEMENT, otherwise N/0/TILE_MEMORY_ID. TSHR valid and stored address do not participate in selection; use the entry's state[54:52], sharers[19:4], and owner[3:0]. All message addresses always come from dc2_message_address. The requester bitmap q has the bit corresponding to source set to 1 among its 16 bits; the owner bitmap o and memory bitmap m are analogous, with bit0 corresponding to tile0. k is the number of set bits in the selected sharers modulo 16, so ffff counts as 0. dc3_pending is message_valid OR instr_request_pending; pending_address takes the dc2 address when message_valid=1, otherwise it unconditionally takes the instr address. All outputs are combinational; selection and counting are not gated by valid, reset, or network available. Conflicting hits follow the priority above; all 8 states, 32 message types, and full-width metadata are allowed. The owner/source range is 0..15; do not add system consistency assumptions.

atoms.title: GETS/GETM state and data actions
atoms.definition: State encodings N=0,M=1,S=2,I=3,S_D=4,MN_A=5,NS_D=6,SN_A=7. GETS=0: N transitions to NS_D, adds q, allocates TSHR, and sends FWD_GETS to memory; M transitions to S_D, adds q and o, sets owner to TILE_ID, allocates TSHR and sets cache validity to 0, and sends FWD_GETS to the old owner; S or I transitions to S, adds q, updates cache, and sends a DATA response to q. GETM=1: N transitions to M, sets owner to source, updates cache, and sends FWD_GETM to memory; M remains M but sets owner to source, updates cache, and sends FWD_GETM to the old owner; S transitions to M, sets owner to source, clears sharers to 0, updates cache, sends DATA to q and INV to the old sharers; I transitions to M, sets owner to source, updates cache and sends DATA to q. GETS/GETM in other states produces no protocol action and preserves metadata. Compute results combinationally after selecting metadata; all destinations, counts, and message selections read state/sharers/owner from before the action. Even if source is already in sharers or equals owner, updates are still requested according to the actions above; see below for valid gating of whether actions take effect. There is no internal directory storage across cycles.

atoms.title: PUTS/PUTM and DATA returns
atoms.definition: PUTS=2: N/M/I/NS_D only send PUTACK to q; S removes q, transitions to I when k=1, otherwise remains S, and updates cache, sending PUTACK to q in either case; S_D/SN_A remove q and edit TSHR, and send PUTACK to q; otherwise no action. PUTM=3: N/I/NS_D only send PUTACK; M always sends PUTACK, and only when source equals owner does it transition to I, set owner to TILE_ID, save input message_data, and update cache; S removes q, updates cache, and sends PUTACK only for a non-owner; S_D always sends PUTACK, and only for a non-owner removes q and retires TSHR while updating cache; MN_A always sends PUTACK, and when sent by the owner additionally generates the WB enable condition but does not change metadata; otherwise no action. DATA=9: S_D or NS_D transitions to S, saves message_data, retires TSHR, and updates cache; otherwise no action. All are combinational actions; the PUTM WB enable is sampled separately at the clock edge. A single sharer is determined by k=1, with no additional constraint on whether q is actually in sharers. The non-owner branch of PUTM in S_D retires TSHR even if the next state remains S_D; do not replace this behavior with speculation about abstract state stability. A PUTM in state S whose source is the owner produces no PUTACK.

atoms.title: Replacement, flush, ACK, and default behavior
atoms.definition: REPLACEMENT=12: I transitions to MN_A, allocates TSHR, and sends a WB response to memory; S transitions to SN_A, allocates TSHR, sends a WB response to memory and RECALL to the old sharers; M transitions to MN_A, allocates TSHR, and sends RECALL to the old owner; otherwise no action. DIR_FLUSH=13: I only sends a WB response to memory; S transitions to I, updates cache, and sends a WB response to memory; M only sends FWD_FLUSH to the old owner; otherwise no action. MC_ACK=14: MN_A or SN_A transitions to N, retires TSHR and sets TSHR entry.valid=0 and cache validity=0, without updating cache; otherwise no action. WB_GEN=16 sends a WB response to memory in all states, with metadata unchanged. All other message encodings and unlisted state/request combinations produce no protocol action, retain the selected metadata and cache data, and default cache validity to 1. The protocol is a combinational function. Unlisted combinations still execute the pending, PLRU, payload, and unconditional WB sampling rules; not all outputs are zero. There are no SIMULATION, COHERENCE_INJECTION, or DISPLAY_COHERENCE macros; undisclosed internal diagnostics are not required. Replacement suppresses cache updates even on a cache hit.

atoms.title: TSHR and cache command combinations
atoms.definition: The protocol actions above are divided into cache update, TSHR allocation, TSHR edit, TSHR retirement, TSHR discard on ACK, and no action. For a cache update or TSHR retirement, message_valid and non-REPLACEMENT cause cache_enable=1; on retirement, TSHR_enable also takes message_valid. For TSHR allocation, TSHR_enable=message_valid and index takes tshr_empty_index; cache_enable is asserted only when message_valid and non-REPLACEMENT and cache_hit. For edit/discard on ACK, only TSHR_enable=message_valid, cache_enable=0. All other enables are 0. Except for allocation, the TSHR index always takes dc2_message_tshr_index. The TSHR payload from high to low is valid, next_state, dc2 address, next_sharers, next_owner; valid is 1 only for allocation or edit actions, even when message_valid=0. cache state/sharers/owner/data take the post-action metadata; data defaults to cache_data and takes message_data only when saving is specified; validity defaults to 1 and is 0 only for GETS/M and MC_ACK/MN_A or SN_A. Enables and payloads are all combinational; payloads are not forced to 0 when enables are 0. Actions are determined only by the current metadata and message type. cache set=dc2 address[12:6], tag=dc2 address[31:13], way=cache_way; the TSHR stored address always uses the dc2 address, ignoring input entry.address.

atoms.title: PLRU and replacement queue
atoms.definition: dc3_update_plru_en always equals dc2_message_valid; the PLRU set takes dc2 address[12:6], and way takes cache_way. dc3_replacement_enqueue is 1 only when cache_enable=1, cache_hit=0, and cache_valid=1. The replacement payload is always formed from cache metadata, independently of enqueue: from high to low, cache_data, dc2_message_source, cache_tag, dc2 address index, 6-bit zero offset, cache_state, cache_sharers, cache_owner. All outputs are combinational; for an invalid message the PLRU enable is 0, but the payload remains defined. For a REPLACEMENT message, cache_enable is always 0, so it is not enqueued into the replacement queue again; a TSHR hit does not mask cache metadata as the replacement victim payload.

atoms.title: Forwarding arbitration and payload
atoms.definition: When message_valid and the protocol has a forwarding action, coherence forwarding has priority: valid=1, and the 43-bit payload from high to low is dc2 source, 4-bit type, dc2 address, uncoherent=0, requestor=0; types are FWD_GETS=4/FWD_GETM=5/INV=6/RECALL=8/FWD_FLUSH=15, and the destinations are determined by the actions above. Otherwise, when instr_request_pending and network_available, an instruction request is sent: valid=1, source=TILE_ID, type=4, address=instr address, uncoherent=1, requestor=1, destinations=memory bitmap, and instr_dequeue=1. In all other cases, forwarding valid, payload, destinations, and dequeue are all 0. In the coherence branch, dequeue=0. Arbitration is combinational; coherence forwarding is not gated by network_available. When a valid message does not require forwarding, instruction forwarding can still be sent in the same cycle. There is no ready-based hold protocol; arbitration is redone immediately when inputs change. Priority blocks instruction dequeue only when there is actual coherence forwarding.

atoms.title: Response payload and invalid window
atoms.definition: dc3_response_valid is only message_valid and the protocol producing a response. The 624-bit response from high to low is: 512-bit data, 64-bit all-ones dirty_mask, 4-bit dc2 source, 4-bit packet_type, 32-bit dc2 address, 4-bit k, from_directory=1, uncoherent=0, requestor=0. data takes cache_data on cache_hit and non-REPLACEMENT, otherwise message_data; this selection differs from the selection of data saved to cache by the protocol. packet_type is PUTACK=7, DATA=9, or WB=11, and is 0 when there is no response action; has_data is 1 only for DATA/WB actions and is not gated by message_valid. The response destinations are q or memory as described above, defaulting to the old sharers when there is no response action. The response payload, has_data, and destinations remain defined by the combinational rules above when response_valid=0, and must not all be cleared to zero or excluded from comparison. With 16 sharers, k=0; DIR_FLUSH still uses cache_data on a cache hit, and REPLACEMENT still uses message_data on a cache hit. There is no response backpressure or holding across cycles.
